Create a diagram on the 1920×1200 canvas that explains how swallows circle upward in a thermal. Show a small group of swallows in motion, each at a different point of a banked turn, so the viewer can infer a continuous climb rather than a row of unrelated bird portraits. Let smooth, generous curves carry the explanation: the shared spiral of their flight, the smaller changes of direction between birds, and the arcing wing and tail shapes that make each pose read as a swallow. Vary the birds’ orientation and wing position—one gliding, one banking with a raised wing, another briefly flapping—while keeping their paths connected to the same rising movement.

Make the flight paths easy to distinguish from the bird silhouettes. Where paths cross, use spacing or a clear break so the route remains legible; use arrowheads only if they help clarify direction. Include a restrained indication of upward airflow around the thermal, but don’t let it become a second subject. Keep any labels brief and useful, identifying the rising air or direction of travel rather than narrating the whole scene. Prioritize a readable relationship between the birds, their curved routes, and the upward motion. Give each bird enough separation to read individually while allowing the flight paths to echo one another; preserve an uncluttered visual hierarchy.
